question: What economic policies did Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi propose in 2025?
text:
Sanae Takaichi’s 2025 economic agenda paired **short-term relief from rising prices** with **longer-term public investment to raise wages and growth**. She called this “responsible and proactive” fiscal policy: spend now on targeted measures, while aiming to lower Japan’s debt-to-GDP ratio by growing the economy faster than public debt. ([japan.kantei.go.jp](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/104/statement/202510/24shoshinhyomei.html?bsft_aaid=72bb9dec-3452-4075-a63c-0f8d60246a1e&bsft_clkid=6c18bd80-303b-4b98-82b0-10f2840e1d39&bsft_eid=a30f775d-a95b-4704-ba5b-9fcd5291f465&bsft_ek=2026-02-16T05%3A00%3A34Z&bsft_lx=6&bsft_mid=90fc3602-ddfd-451c-96a8-cc6e033e1f1c&bsft_mime_type=html&bsft_tv=1285&bsft_txnid=e39b4aa0-5748-470d-98fc-2b389a8e2054&bsft_uid=54e33523-d5da-4f6c-adb8-c5cdeb30b16d&bsft_utid=54e33523-d5da-4f6c-adb8-c5cdeb30b16d-Newsletter_COR_WHATEVERITTAKES&utm_source=openai))

- **Cost-of-living relief.** Her government proposed ending the temporary gasoline and diesel tax surcharges, subsidizing winter electricity and gas bills, paying **¥20,000 per child**, and giving local governments more money to help households with rising food prices. ([bf.emb-japan.go.jp](https://www.bf.emb-japan.go.jp/files/100943314.pdf))
- **Income-tax relief.** In December, her government proposed raising the annual income-tax threshold from **¥1.6 million to ¥1.78 million** and linking key deductions to inflation. It also began designing a refundable tax credit for low- and middle-income households. ([investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-to-raise-taxfree-income-threshold-to-ease-inflation-squeeze-4414532?utm_source=openai))
- **Higher wages and business investment.** She proposed helping small businesses invest in labor-saving equipment and pass higher costs on to customers so they could afford wage increases. She also backed public-private investment in AI, semiconductors, shipbuilding, and quantum technology, along with stronger supply chains for critical materials. ([japan.kantei.go.jp](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/104/statement/202510/24shoshinhyomei.html?bsft_aaid=72bb9dec-3452-4075-a63c-0f8d60246a1e&bsft_clkid=6c18bd80-303b-4b98-82b0-10f2840e1d39&bsft_eid=a30f775d-a95b-4704-ba5b-9fcd5291f465&bsft_ek=2026-02-16T05%3A00%3A34Z&bsft_lx=6&bsft_mid=90fc3602-ddfd-451c-96a8-cc6e033e1f1c&bsft_mime_type=html&bsft_tv=1285&bsft_txnid=e39b4aa0-5748-470d-98fc-2b389a8e2054&bsft_uid=54e33523-d5da-4f6c-adb8-c5cdeb30b16d&bsft_utid=54e33523-d5da-4f6c-adb8-c5cdeb30b16d-Newsletter_COR_WHATEVERITTAKES&utm_source=openai))

The centerpiece was the **November 21, 2025 stimulus package**: **¥21.3 trillion** in new fiscal measures, including tax cuts, or **¥25.5 trillion** once government investment and loan programs were included. ([japan.kantei.go.jp](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/104/statement/202511/21kaiken.html?utm_source=openai))
